job.style: a passage rich in numbers, dates or measurements

passage: India is a land of diverse physical features shaped over millions of years. The Himalayas, which stretch about 2,400 kilometres, are not static; they are young fold mountains that continue to rise due to tectonic plate movements. The Northern Plains were formed by the interplay of three major river systems—the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra—which deposited vast amounts of fertile alluvium over a long period. Unlike the plains, the Peninsular Plateau is a tableland composed of old crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks, featuring rolling surfaces and shallow valleys rather than being a flat, featureless area. In the western part of India lies the Indian Desert, which is an undulating sandy plain. While it receives very low rainfall, it is not completely devoid of water, as it contains seasonal streams and some small oases. The geological formation of India is a result of complex processes involving the movement of the Indo-Australian plate towards the Eurasian plate. These movements have created the varied landscape we see today, from the towering northern peaks to the coastal plains and the islands of Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar groups.

items.evidence: The Himalayas, which stretch about 2,400 kilometres, are not static; they are young fold mountains that continue to rise due to tectonic plate movements.
items.q: A Himalayan peak is measured again after many years. What would the climbers most likely find?
options: It has grown slightly taller over time
It has stayed exactly the same height
It has worn down because it is very old
It has sunk lower as plates pull apart
items.explain: The Himalayas are young fold mountains that keep rising because tectonic plates keep moving.

wrong.why: thinks the Himalayas are old mountains wearing away
reverses the effect of plate movement

items.evidence: The Northern Plains were formed by the interplay of three major river systems—the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra—which deposited vast amounts of fertile alluvium over a long period.
items.q: How did the Northern Plains come to be covered with rich, fertile soil?
options: Three river systems laid down silt over ages
Himalayan rocks broke down with no river help
Hard plateau rock slowly cracked into soil
The Ganga alone flooded it in one season
items.explain: The Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra deposited fertile alluvium over a long period to form the plains.

wrong.why: thinks Himalayan erosion alone made the plains
thinks the plains are made of hard rock
picks one nearby river name and ignores the long time

items.evidence: Unlike the plains, the Peninsular Plateau is a tableland composed of old crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks, featuring rolling surfaces and shallow valleys rather than being a flat, featureless area.
items.q: Meena says the Peninsular Plateau is completely flat and featureless. Which fact shows Meena is wrong?
options: It has gently rolling land and shallow valleys
It has young layers of soft river soil
It has tall, young fold mountains rising
It has deep layers of fertile alluvium
items.explain: The plateau is a tableland of old rocks with rolling surfaces and shallow valleys, not a flat area.

wrong.why: thinks the plateau is a young landform
mixes up the plateau with the Himalayas
mixes up the plateau with the Northern Plains

items.evidence: While it receives very low rainfall, it is not completely devoid of water, as it contains seasonal streams and some small oases.
items.q: Which would a traveller most likely see while crossing the Indian Desert?
options: Small oases and streams in some seasons
Dry sand with no water source at all
Wide rivers flowing all through the year
Thick forests watered by heavy rainfall
items.explain: The desert gets very little rain but still has seasonal streams and some small oases.

wrong.why: thinks a desert has no water at all
mixes up the desert with the river plains
